correctness.rationale: Every weak component contains one cycle, so cycle-indicator expectations give the exact mean count. Marking an r-component makes the remaining n-r map uniform; the mixed moment follows, including r=n with the empty-map convention. Strict mean monotonicity proves the finite sign switch. A Gaussian product expansion uniform at j=O(sqrt(n) log n), summable remainder, and a smooth Riemann-sum difference yield the order-sqrt(n) threshold with the displayed constant. The extracted standard-library verifier passes 3386 assertions, supporting but not proving the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Conditional sensitivity of the total component count to a component size is a natural dependency statistic for functional digraph fragmentation. The exact full-spectrum monotone sign law identifies an intrinsic large-component transition, while the nonzero sqrt(n) displacement provides an essential second-order location beyond first-order 0.86466 n. This is neither a single parameter substitution nor a mere recomputation of the known leading logarithmic mean count.
